title: The Lion's Share
text:
A lion once made a hunting partnership with a few weaker animals. In the version Phaedrus tells, they were a cow, a goat and a sheep. They agreed to hunt together and share whatever they caught.

Together they brought down a large stag. The lion took charge of the division and carefully cut the carcass into four parts. Then he explained the arrangement. "The first part is mine because I am called the lion. The second you will grant me because I am brave. The third comes to me because I am the strongest. And as for the fourth, woe to anyone who touches it."

The other animals looked at the four portions, then at the lion's teeth and claws. None of them moved. They had done their share of the running and the work, and they went home with nothing. The lion dragged the whole stag away, and the phrase "the lion's share" has meant the biggest piece, taken by force, ever since.
lesson: Before you join a partnership, look at who will divide the results and what will hold them to the deal. A promise of fairness from someone far stronger than you is only as good as their character.
